subject: Partner affiliation rules & mapping: Hartwell Financial overlap
messages:
From: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Hi Sergio / Camila,

Quick note — Hartwell Financial reached out last week for a proof-of-concept on model inference cost optimization. They told us they also have a separate contact working with Adept Analytics on integration architecture. Nimbus has been engaged on the consulting side (security review + infra recommendations) and we see a potential conflict as both partners have active opportunities.

Can we get a quick alignment on who owns commercial/non-commercial tracks? Hartwell is planning procurement in mid-Jan; we'd like to avoid duplicate outreach. Happy to share our services scope and a short MAP if helpful.

Att: none in this thread yet.

Gary
Gary Lewis
Head of Alliances
Nimbus Consulting
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Thanks Gary — and thanks for flagging this. Looping in Marissa and Tessa to validate any clear partner routing rules.

Camila: can you pull the partner-account mapping and export the engagement timeline for Hartwell? Use the partner_account_matrix template (Ill attach). We need to decide: 1) who owns procurement/contracting conversations, 2) who owns implementation consulting, and 3) whether we require an exclusive route for procurement opportunities. Please mark the contacts at Hartwell you see in CRM and the current opportunity stages.

Marissa / Tessa: any contractual obligations on our side (marketplace-pinned partners, preferred ISV relationships) that would nudge ownership to Adept or Nimbus? If not, propose a temporary ruleset for this account.

Goal: consolidated reply today so we can tell both partners and Hartwell what to expect.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Att: partner_account_matrix.xlsx (stub - 1 worksheet)

Summary from matrix (see attachment):
- Hartwell Financial (AM: Jordan Park) — two active opportunities: POC (Nimbus, stage: Eval) and Procurement (Adept via marketplace, stage: Scoping).
- Nimbus footprint: infra + security review, non-binding SOW discussion started 11/18.
- Adept footprint: integration connector and marketplace listing. Adept is asking to be first-contact for procurement if Marketplace purchase is chosen.
- No signed exclusivity, no partner co-sell contract on file.

Key contacts at Hartwell in CRM: Jordan Park (procurement), Lina Cho (platform eng), Marcus Dell (security).

Recommendation: split ownership by track — allow Adept to lead procurement (marketplace path) but require a co-sell notification and handoff process for any procurement conversations that continue to vendor negotiations. Nimbus should own consulting/SOW discussions and be the primary implementation partner for their SOW. We should capture this in a one-page MAP and record the owner fields in HubSpot.

Camila
Senior Manager, Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Thanks Camila — that split aligns with our general routing rules, with one caveat: Adepts marketplace listing gives them a transactional advantage, which can bypass Sales-assisted procurement if the customer chooses self-serve. If Hartwell moves forward via marketplace we need a clear crediting and revenue-split policy documented before we hand ownership for renewal attribution.

Related: HubSpot record attached for quick reference: https://hubspot.redwood.com/contacts/DEAL-8943 (internal link).

Proposed temporary ruleset: 1) Procurement via marketplace = Adept primary for contract execution; Redwood Partner Ops to record co-sell alert and create a Partner Services order for Nimbus if the customer requests consulting. 2) Any procurement that escalates to negotiated T&Cs > $200k reverts to Redwood sales + partner compensation review.

If everyone agrees I will draft the short MAP and the revenue-split note for Partner Ops to sign off.

Marissa
Head of Channel Partnerships
From: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Att: mutual_action_plan.docx (stub)

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a short MAP that outlines Nimbuss role on the POC and proposed SOW. Our ask is: 1) if Hartwell buys via Adept marketplace we remain the named implementation partner for the initial engagement and we receive co-sell credit (standard 15% referral margin), 2) Redwood to share procurement contact updates and notify Nimbus at least 48 hours before contract execution.

Were flexible on revenue split but want predictability — the MAP is intentionally short so its easy for Hartwell to sign.

Happy to join a 15-min alignment call if useful.

Gary
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Gary Lewis <g.lewis@nimbus.com>, Adept Analytics <sales@adept-analytics.io>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Jordan Park <j.park@hartwell.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Overlap: Hartwell Financial engagement / who owns the account?

Folks — thanks for the quick inputs. Here's the decision and immediate next steps so we have a clean handoff: 

Decision:
- Procurement track (marketplace/transactional purchase): Adept Analytics will be the primary procurement-facing partner. They will handle the marketplace listing and contract execution for self-serve transactions.
- Consulting & implementation: Nimbus Consulting will remain the primary services partner for the POC and any SOW-based implementations.
- Co-sell & credits: Redwood will credit Nimbus for implementation services when Nimbus is engaged; for marketplace-led procurement we will implement a 15% referral margin to Nimbus for the initial services engagement (per Gary's MAP). Any negotiated contracts > $200k will require Sales involvement and a revenue-split review.

Action items (owners):
- Camila: update partner_account_matrix.xlsx and set the partner_owner fields in HubSpot (DEAL-8943) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: draft a one-page MAP and revenue-split note for Partner Ops review — circulate by Friday.
- Tessa: notify Partner Ops and Partner Legal to prepare a brief addendum if Hartwell elects marketplace procurement.
- Jordan (Hartwell): please confirm preferred procurement path (marketplace vs. direct) so we can finalize the MAP.

I will record this outcome in the partner portal and update the internal routing rules to prevent duplicate outreach across partners for Hartwell. If anyone thinks this is materially unfair to a partner, flag it now; we'll escalate to VP level.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
